profile.headline: I build evaluation infrastructure for LLM systems · Senior SDET @ Cisco Meraki · Evals, calibrated judges, CI release gates
profile.summary:
I build evaluation infrastructure for LLM systems.

Most teams shipping AI features can't answer a basic question: if you change a prompt or swap a model, did it get worse? There's usually no way to tell. Somebody spot-checks a few outputs, it looks fine, it ships.

I build the thing that answers it — deterministic fixtures, calibrated judges, repeatable eval suites wired into CI as release gates. At Cisco Meraki I've built this for the Meraki AI Assistant.

Before AI, over 25 years of quality engineering on hard systems: browser and API automation at scale, CI/CD pipelines, and hardware-in-the-loop testing against real network devices — switches and wireless controllers, pyATS, cross-layer debugging between cloud software and physical hardware.

Portland, Oregon.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer in Test
positions.description:
Quality engineering for cloud network management and AI-enabled
product experiences.
• Built automated evaluation infrastructure for the Cisco Meraki
  AI Assistant — reusable rubrics, deterministic fixtures, judge
  calibration, repeated-trial comparison, and evaluation lanes wired
  into CI as release gates.
• Contributed to the initial shipped integration of Cisco Catalyst
  devices into the Meraki cloud-management platform.
• Built browser and API automation (Cypress, pytest, pyATS) across
  UI, API, and real-device layers for a complex network-management
  product.
• Established a trustworthy regression signal by classifying known
  issues, driving repair-or-retire decisions, and separating product
  defects from automation, lab, and environment failures.
• Improved CI quality infrastructure: parallelized pyATS jobs,
  separated long-running suites, and made device-test failures
  inspectable through retained artifacts and pipeline-visible results.
• Cross-team defect discovery and triage across network device
  onboarding, wireless controllers, configuration, APIs, and UI.
